# DB Hive — System Architecture (initial stub)

## Purpose

This document captures the high-level architecture for DB Hive (MVP). It complements `docs/prd.md` and `docs/frontend-architecture.md` and provides a single-source reference for system components, major data flows, security constraints, deployment and rollback guidance, and integration points.

Refer to: `docs/prd.md`, `docs/frontend-architecture.md`, and `.bmad-core/checklists/po-master-checklist.md` for acceptance criteria and additional elicitation items.

## System overview (high level)

- User-facing frontend: Next.js app (deployed to Vercel / CDN)
- Backend: Serverless query proxy functions (AWS Lambda / Vercel Serverless) that mediate connections to external DBs via ephemeral SSH tunnels
- Primary app DB: NeonDB (serverless Postgres for user metadata, saved queries, audit logs). Local development should prefer connecting to a Neon dev/staging project — no Dockerized Postgres is required for day-to-day development.
- Secrets store: Managed secret manager (AWS Secrets Manager or Vercel environment + encryption)
- LLM adapter: Provider-agnostic adapter layer (OpenAI-compatible interface)
- CI/CD: GitHub Actions / Turborepo or similar; canary deployments + feature flags
- Observability: Centralized logs (CloudWatch / Vercel logs), Sentry for errors, metrics (Prometheus / CloudWatch)
- Offline/Local: Schema upload & parser service with isolated offline workspace storage (encrypted per-user)

## Component diagram (high-level)

```mermaid
graph LR
  Browser[User Browser]
  CDN[CDN]
  Frontend[Next.js App (Vercel)]
  API[Serverless API / Query Proxy]
  SSHProxy[Ephemeral SSH Tunnel Manager]
  ExternalDBs[(External DBs\nPostgres / MySQL / etc.)]
  Neon[NeonDB (App DB)]
  Secrets[Secrets Manager]
  LLMAdapter[LLM Adapter]
  CI[CI / Canary Pipeline]
  Monitoring[Monitoring & Logs]

  Browser -->|HTTPS| CDN --> Frontend
  Frontend -->|HTTP API / GraphQL| API
  API -->|establish tunnel / run query| SSHProxy
   SSHProxy -->|SSH| ExternalDBs
   %% Note: NeonDB connections use normal Postgres drivers and do not require SSH tunnels.
  API -->|metadata / saved queries| Neon
  API -->|store/fetch secrets (encrypted)| Secrets
  API -->|LLM calls (audit + rate-limit)| LLMAdapter
  CI -->|deploy| Frontend
  CI -->|deploy| API
  Frontend --> Monitoring
  API --> Monitoring
```

Notes:

- The Query Proxy is the single integration point that encapsulates SSH lifecycle, query execution, budgeting and LLM adapter calls. Keep the proxy minimal and well-instrumented.
- The SSH tunnel manager should create ephemeral, scoped tunnels per-request or per-session and avoid long-lived credentials on the backend.

## Key data flows

1. Connection test (schema discovery)
   - Browser -> Frontend -> API: request `connection.test` with connection metadata (and optionally client-side encrypted key)
   - API -> Secrets: retrieve/decrypt stored credential (if stored)
   - API -> SSHProxy: open ephemeral tunnel and request schema
   - SSHProxy -> ExternalDB: run `SELECT`-only schema introspection
   - Response returned back to Frontend and shown in the Schema Explorer

2. Query execution (read-only sandbox)
   - Frontend sends visual_spec / SQL + execution options (timeout, row-limit)
   - API validates, enforces sandbox (read-only), and routes to SSHProxy
   - For large results: API streams chunked responses to Frontend and triggers server-side pagination
   - All executions emit audit events to NeonDB and logs to Monitoring

3. LLM assistance flow
   - Frontend requests suggestion with context (visual_spec, sample schema)
   - API enforces rate limits, budget checks and sanitizes prompts
   - API calls LLMAdapter which sends to the configured provider
   - LLM response is audited (prompt & result references) and returned to the Frontend for user opt-in

4. Offline schema upload
   - User uploads `.sql` or JSON schema
   - Parser service validates, returns parsed schema and warnings
   - Parsed schema is stored encrypted under the user's workspace for offline queries

## Security & secrets model

- Secrets at rest: Use provider-managed secrets manager (AWS Secrets Manager / Vercel env) with encryption keys and access policies.
- Client-side encryption: For higher assurance, allow client-side encryption of SSH private keys before upload; server stores encrypted blob and never has plaintext.
- Ephemeral tunnels: Avoid long-lived backend SSH sessions — create per-request ephemeral tunnels with limited lifetime and scope.
- Least privilege: Query proxy runs with only necessary permissions; external DB connections default to read-only roles and explicit audit for any elevated flows.
- Audit & compliance: Store audit logs (connection events, query hashes, LLM prompts) in NeonDB with retention and export mechanisms.

## Deployment, canary & rollback strategy

- Canary deployment: Deploy to a canary route (feature-flagged) and promote after health checks and telemetry pass. Use short-lived canaries and progressive traffic ramp.
- Rolling rollback: Use feature flags to quickly disable new UI/flows. For infra changes, revert IaC changes and redeploy previous artifacts as a controlled rollback.
- DB migrations: Prefer backward-compatible migrations. Any breaking migration requires a migration plan: backup snapshot, migration script with dry-run, and rollback SQL.
- Runbook (per release): health-checks, rollback steps, how to toggle feature flags, and contacts for on-call.

Minimal rollback checklist (per deployment):

- Confirm health checks for canary route (HTTP status, telemetry events)
- If SLO breach or errors, toggle feature flag to disable new flow
- Revert IaC changes only after validating that revert will not break data migrations
- Restore DB snapshot only as last resort after stakeholder approval

## IaC skeleton & recommended project layout

Recommended top-level layout (suggested):

```text
infra/
   terraform/             # reusable modules and envs (or pulumi/)
   ci/                    # deployment scripts for CI (canary, promos)
   manifests/             # k8s manifests (if used) or cloudformation
frontend/                # Next.js app
backend/                 # serverless functions (query proxy, parsers)
tests/                   # e2e + integration fixtures (ssh-simulator)
docs/                    # architecture + runbooks
```

Recommended IaC tools: Terraform (with workspaces) or Pulumi. For small MVP, minimal Terraform modules + CI promotion workflows are sufficient.

---

## Observability & SLOs

- Telemetry events (must emit): `onboarding.start`, `connection.test.succeeded`, `first_query.success`, `first_query.failure`, `llm.suggestion.requested`, `llm.suggestion.applied`.
- Key metrics: query latency (P50/P95), query error rate, canary success rate, LLM usage (tokens / cost), active connections count.
- Alerts: high error-rate on canary, elevated LLM token spend, repeated SSH tunnel failures, and high query durations.
- Logs: Structured logs from API and Frontend with correlation IDs for requests and query executions.

---

## Testing strategy

- Unit tests for frontend and backend modules
- Integration tests for query proxy flows should run against a Neon test/staging instance where possible. For validating SSH-tunneled external DB discovery and schema flows use a non-Docker integration simulator harness (or remote managed test endpoint) in CI. Avoid relying on local Docker images for core integration tests to reduce onboarding friction.
- Playwright E2E tests for the canary path (create connection → test → build query → run → export)
- Scheduled integration test runs for migrations and canary promotion
